pr.body:
Admits exactly one further embedded-audit pair, grok-cli / grok-4.7, on owner instruction 'admit grok 4.7' (2026-11-10), motivated by PR #1503 whose governing audit ran on grok-4.7. The existing grok-cli / grok-4.5 pair stays valid.

Fail-closed in both directions: auditor_model grok-4.7 requires auditor_tool grok-cli (new conditional), and auditor_tool grok-cli requires auditor_model in {grok-4.5, grok-4.7} (the existing conditional changed from const to enum). Both carry then.required. One enum member added (auditor_model grok-4.7); auditor_tool enum unchanged. grok-4.6, aliases and -build labels are not admitted.

Backward compatibility is proven at class level by a hermetic differential against a hash-pinned copy of the pre-change schema (c5a0ca34f) over every pre-change tool/model pair and all five statuses, plus a test that the only newly valid inputs are grok-cli/grok-4.7 for non-SKIPPED statuses.

Scope was set by a deterministic consumer inventory (proof bundle). legacy.py's provider table is keyed by tool only and already maps grok-cli; local_audit_acceptance.py and validate_audit_proof.py are schema-driven; run_embedded_audit.py has no recognition table. Changed beyond the schema: the parity corpus (conditional count 7 to 8 plus five rows), the grok-4.5 suite's exact-surface assertion, and the kimi suite's enum-membership filter, which misread the grok conditional's new then-enum as lost enum membership.

This packet is not yet audited; an independent audit not run on grok-4.7 is required before merge.
